column1: HOW TO ADD OR CHANGE ITEMS IN THE MVP PRICE LIST
The app reads the first tab (the price list) about every 10 minutes and checks it before using it. This tab is just instructions — the app ignores it.

column2: Go to the price list tab and add a new row at the bottom.
Fill in every column (see the table below). Don't leave a price empty.
Wait up to 10 minutes, or in the app go to Office → Price list → Sync now.
Check the message in Office → Price list: ✓ means it's live. A red box tells you which row to fix — until then the app keeps the old prices.
WHAT TO PUT
A new code nobody else uses. Start with the trade: EL- (electrical), HV- (heating & cooling), PL- (plumbing), then a number.
Exactly one of: Electrical, HVAC, Plumbing
A group name. Techs see items grouped by it (Panel, Drains, Motors, Replacement…).
What the job is, in plain words. Customers see this on estimates.
Estimated hours (for reference only).
Price for non-members. Numbers only — no $ needed.
Price for members. Can't be higher than standard_price. Put 0 if the membership includes it.
Service = repairs and small jobs. Install = replacements and new installs.
Leave EMPTY for repairs. For replacements: Small ($100), Medium ($250) or Large ($500) member credit.
Optional. Internal note shown to techs.
Just edit the number in the cell. Reports and estimates already sent to customers keep the old price.
Delete its row. The app won't allow removing an item that the check-up guide or the service call still uses — it will say which one.
Don't change, move or rename the first row of the price list (the column names).
Don't rename or move the price list tab. Keep it as the FIRST tab.
Each code only once. Don't reuse a code from a deleted item for something different.
EL-100, HV-100 and PL-100 are the service calls ($19 members / $119 non-members). Don't delete them.
Service calls: the $119 is never credited toward the repair. Joining the club is the only way to get $19.
Right away — techs find it under “+ Add items from the price book”.
Only when a check-up finding points to its code. Ask to add or change a finding in the Inspection Guide.
Editors: owner and office. Trades: Viewer or Commenter (they see prices, suggest changes with comments).
Every change the app publishes is listed in Office → Price list → History (what changed, when, by whom).
